paragraphs: Rabbi Ilai. The sages told Rabbi Abbahu, “Show us where Rabbi Ilai is hidden” (he was hiding, and the students did not know). He replied, “He rejoiced with a maiden” (was happy with her at night, and now sleeps), “an Aaronite” (a priest’s daughter), “a latter one” (his first wife died; this was the latter), “graceful” [עירנית; the source explains “possessing charm”]. Some say a tractate: “Aaronite” (Seder Kodashim, Aaron’s service), “a latter one” (he finished another and began this), “deep and difficult” [עירנית]. They asked Rabbi Ilai where Rabbi Abbahu was hidden. He replied, “He consulted with the one who crowns,” etc., Eruvin 53b. Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, and Rabbi Ilai sat. Rabbi Abba told them, etc.; Rabbi Ilai said, “Thus Rav said,” etc.; “Go to Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakum and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat,” Bava Kamma 117b. Yuchasin lists Rabbi Ila, Rabbi Yirmeyah, Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi, Rabbi Elazar, and Rabbi Shimon; he writes perhaps this is Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish or Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, but gives no location. I think they are the ones above. Rabbi Shimon is Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakum; Rabbi Ilai [ור׳ אלעאי; wording compressed] is an error, as is Rabbi Yirmeyah.

Know that Yuchasin writes Rabbi Elai [אלעאי] and Rabbi Il'ai with yod [אילעאי]. Rashi, Bekhorot 42b, writes there were two Rabbi Ilais. Therefore I have recorded who lived in their times, or their teachers and students.

Rabbi Abba (see there), and see Rabbi Abba bar Acha; Rabbi Abbahu (see there). He challenges Abaye, Menachot 25a. Rabbi Avin said in Rabbi Ilai’s name, from Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, Yevamot 65b—several things. Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat (see there). Jerusalem Talmud, Terumot, chapter 2, halakhah 1: Rabbi Le'ai says from Rabbi Liezer. Beginning of Demai: Rabbi Layya from Rabbi Liezer. Rav Beruna; Rabbi Zeira, Menachot 25a. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said, etc.; Rabbi Ilai from Rabbi Chiyya bar Yose, Bava Metzia 117a. Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi (see there). In Rabbi Chanina’s name, Chullin 24b; he said Rabbi Chanina ruled in Sepphoris, there 25b; Eruvin 28b. Yuchasin writes Rabbi Chanina apparently was his teacher. But Bava Kamma 65b: Rabbi Chanina objected to Rabbi Il'ai, etc.; he told him, etc.; “May the Merciful save us from this opinion!” He replied, “On the contrary, may the Merciful save us,” etc. Shabbat 84, end of a: Rabbi Il'ai objects; Rabbi Chanina tells him, etc.; “May the Merciful save us,” etc.; “On the contrary,” etc. Ketubbot 45b likewise: Rabbi Chanina tells him, etc.; “May the Merciful save us,” etc.; “On the contrary,” etc. If Rabbi Chanina was his teacher, how could he object to his student? How could the student tell his teacher, “May the Merciful save us,” etc., disparaging words? From Rabbi Yehudah bar Misperet; in Rabbi Yehudah bar Safra’s name. In Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Shabbat 5a; Ellu Tereifot 50, end of a; Chelek. Rabbi Yochanan ben Elyakum—see there; Rabbi Yonatan. In Rabbi Yose ben Zimri’s name; Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha (see there); in Rabbi Yishmael’s name, Bekhorot 41b. In Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha’s name, from our master, Berakhot 49a. There 22a: Rabbi Il'ai said in Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov’s name from our master. He told Ulla, “Give my greetings to Rav Beruna, my brother” (see there). In Rav’s name, Shabbat 142a; Eruvin 3a, 14a. Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakum (see there). In Resh Lakish’s name, Ketubbot 49b; Zevachim 114a; Shabbat 28b. Yuchasin lists Rabbi Il'ai, Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, and Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavda; I did not find it. Perhaps it is Kiddushin 33b: Rabbi Ila and Rabbi Yaakov bar Zavdi stood before Rabbi Shimon bar Abba.
